sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by membrane-impermeable SNAP-dye labeling in live HEK 293T cells; agonist (1 mM glutamate)-induced internalization and colocalization with GFP-2xFYVE (endosome) and Lamp1-YFP (lysosome) markers demonstrated; N-terminally SNAP-tagged constructs used for all electrophysiology recordings (function preserved); rat HA-tagged mGluR8 at same position functional in Gα15-coupled calcium assays.
sites.rationale: All ledger lines describing N-terminal tags on mGluR8 (L1, L3, L4, L9–L13) converge on the same architectural position: a tag placed after the signal peptide and before the mature receptor sequence. The native human mGluR8 SP spans residues 1–33 (computed landmarks), so insert_after_residue = 33 (S), with residue_after = 34 (Q), placing the tag at the extracellular N-terminus of the large Venus flytrap domain (34–583), 550 residues from TM1. Python verification confirms S at position 33 and Q at position 34. The position is topology-derived because no ledger line names a specific residue number for the N-terminal junction, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists and the construct architecture is unambiguous. Human mGluR8 constructs were built with a heterologous N-terminal signal peptide (rat mGluR5) followed by HA and SNAP tags (or FLAG and CLIP tags) upstream of the full-length human mGluR8 sequence in pRK5. The heterologous SP drives the tag to the extracellular face; in the canonical human sequence the native SP ends at residue 33 (S), so the tag is placed between residue 33 and the mature N-terminus at residue 34 (Q). Surface display was confirmed by labeling with membrane-impermeable fluorophores (SNAP-Surface dyes), and agonist-induced internalization and colocalization with endosomal/lysosomal markers were demonstrated in live and fixed HEK 293T cells (L5–L8). The same N-terminally SNAP-tagged constructs were used for all electrophysiology recordings (L13), and the rat ortholog HA-tagged at the same position was used in calcium-mobilization functional assays (L1).

sources.claim: All SNAP-tagged mGluR8 (human) constructs were generated with an N-terminal signal peptide from rat mGluR5 followed by HA- and SNAP-tags in the pRK5 vector as previously described 54 .

literature_notes: All thirteen ledger lines describe tags at one of two positions: (1) the extracellular N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage (L1, L3–L13), or (2) the intracellular C-terminus (L1 RLuc8, L2 HiBiT). No ledger line reports a tag inserted into any extracellular loop or inter-domain linker of mGluR8. The N-terminal site is supported by multiple independent papers using HA, SNAP, CLIP, FLAG, Halo, and HA+FLAG tags on both rat and human mGluR8, with surface display and functional validation. L11 describes a cryo-EM construct with N-terminal HA+FLAG+AAA on full-length membrane-anchored human mGluR8, further confirming the position. The heterologous rat mGluR5 signal peptide used in L3/L4/L9/L10/L12/L13 replaces the native SP but delivers the tag to the same extracellular face; the insert_after_residue is assigned to 33 (the last residue of the native human SP) because that is the canonical junction in the UniProt sequence. position_evidence is 'topology_derived' because no clip names a residue number for the N-terminal junction — only the construct architecture (SP → tag → mGluR8) is stated.

literature_other_positions.note: HiBiT tag (VSGWRLFKKIS) fused C-terminally after a GSPPARAT linker; the C-terminus of mGluR8 is intracellular (residues 844–908 per topology landmarks), so this is not a surface tag site.
Split RLuc8 fragments (L1 residues 1–229 or L2 residues 230–311) fused C-terminally after a GSPPARAT linker on rat mGluR8; C-terminus is intracellular, not a surface site.
